rules.name: Employee is subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee who lives outside Switzerland is subject to source tax regardless of nationality. An employee who lives in Switzerland is subject only if they are not Swiss, do not hold a C permit, and are not married to a Swiss national or C-permit holder who lives in Switzerland. Only employees who are subject answer the source tax questions.
inputs: Spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit
rules.expression: (is_set(address_country) and address_country != "Switzerland") or (address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and permit_type != "C permit" and is_set(civil_status) and not (civil_status == "Married" and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_permit_type == "C permit") and spouse_residence_country == "Switzerland") and (civil_status != "Married" or is_set(spouse_nationality)))

rules.name: Pension insurance start date
rules.statement: The insurance start date is derived from the first working day, not asked. If the first working day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day. Otherwise it starts on the 1st of the following month. If the first working day changes, the insurance start date must be derived again and the pension fund's date corrected. The result is always the 1st of a month, as the pension fund requires.

table.then: Insurance starts on the first working day

when: is not the 1st of a month
table.then: Insurance starts on the 1st of the following month (e.g. 15.03 gives 01.04)

rules.name: Civil status answer for the source tax calculator
rules.statement: The source tax calculator's civil status question is answered from the employee's civil status, not asked again: Married maps to 'married or registered partnership' (Verheiratet oder eingetragene Partnerschaft). Single, Divorced and Widowed map to 'single, divorced, separated, widowed' (Ledig, Geschieden, Getrennt, Verwitwet).
rules.expression: if_else(civil_status == "Married", "Married or registered partnership", if_else(is_set(civil_status), "Single, divorced, separated, widowed", null))

rules.name: Residence answers for the source tax calculator
rules.statement: The calculator's 'main residence in Switzerland?' and 'country of residence' questions are answered from the country of the home address, not asked again: Switzerland gives main residence in Switzerland. Germany and Liechtenstein give that country. Any other country gives 'other country' (Anderes Land). Switzerland and other countries give the base tariff without more residence questions.

table.then: Main residence in Switzerland: no. Country of residence: Germany (Germany questions follow)
Main residence in Switzerland: no. Country of residence: Liechtenstein (Liechtenstein questions follow)
Main residence in Switzerland: no. Country of residence: other country (base tariff)

rules.expression: if_else(address_country == "Switzerland", "Switzerland", if_else(address_country == "Germany", "Germany", if_else(address_country == "Liechtenstein", "Liechtenstein", if_else(is_set(address_country), "Other country", null))))

rules.name: Church-tax suffix of the tariff
rules.statement: For earned income, the employee's denomination sets the church-tax suffix of the source tax tariff: Y for Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed, N for none or other (e.g. A0Y vs A0N). Replacement income tariffs (G/Q) have no suffix.

when: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed

rules.expression: if_else(income_type == "Replacement income", null, if_else(confession == "Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed", "Y", if_else(confession == "None or other", "N", null)))

rules.name: Base tariff letter (source tax)
rules.statement: The calculator's base tariff letter: replacement income gives G. Married with a working spouse gives C, married with a non-working spouse gives B. Not married gives A, or H if at least one child is counted with H (child in household, and sole custody or the employee is the main contributor). For employees in Germany the cross-border tariff replaces A→L, B→M, C→N, H→P, G→Q when it applies. The tariff digit is the number of counted children. HR keeps the calculator as the authority for the final tariff.
rules.expression: if_else(income_type == "Replacement income", "G", if_else(income_type == "Earned income" and civil_status == "Married", if_else(spouse_gainful_employment == "yes", "C", if_else(spouse_gainful_employment == "no", "B", null)), if_else(income_type == "Earned income" and is_set(civil_status), if_else(child_custody == "Sole custody" or (child_same_household == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "The employee"), "H", "A"), null)))

rules.name: Questionnaire flow overview
rules.statement: The questionnaire runs in this order, each step only with the questions that apply: 1 Personal details (first name, last name, date of birth). 2 Home address (street, house number, postcode, town, country, and the canton if the employee lives in Switzerland). 3 Employment start (confirm the first working day, from which the insurance start date is derived). 4 Nationality and permit (only if the employee lives in Switzerland: nationality, and the permit if not Swiss). 5 Family (civil status. Spouse's date of birth if married. Spouse's nationality, permit and residence only if married and otherwise subject to source tax). 6 Source tax (only if subject to source tax: type of income, denomination, spouse works, children and one block per child, then the Germany or Liechtenstein cross-border questions). Address comes before nationality because employees living abroad need no nationality question. Civil status comes before the spouse questions.

open_questions.question: How should an employee in a registered partnership answer civil status, and do the pension fund and the source tax spouse exemption treat them like married employees (partner's date of birth, partner's nationality/permit/residence)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pension fund list (Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed) has no registered partnership, but the calculator groups it with married, and such employees exist (Daniel). Without an answer they cannot be registered correctly.
options: Ask them to choose 'Married' and treat them as married everywhere
Ask the pension fund how to register them and keep a separate answer for source tax
Ask HR to handle it manually
open_questions.recommendation: Ask Pensionskasse Muster via HR. Until then, treat registered partners as Married for both parties, because the calculator explicitly groups them together.

open_questions.question: Which civil status should a separated (still married) employee choose? The calculator groups 'separated' with single, but the pension fund has no such option.
open_questions.why_it_matters: A separated employee would pick Married for the pension fund and get the married source tax path, which may differ from the calculator's grouping.
options: Married for the pension fund, plus an extra 'separated' question for source tax only
open_questions.recommendation: Confirm with HR. Do not add a question until then.

open_questions.question: Does the pension fund ask for any spouse data when civil status is Divorced or Widowed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: No screenshot shows these cases. Asking too little could block the registration.
options: Spouse's date of birth also appears
open_questions.recommendation: Assume no extra fields. Verify with a screenshot of these two cases.

open_questions.question: Does the pension fund's 'Canton' mean canton of residence or of work, and what is entered for employees who live abroad (Germany, Liechtenstein)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The field is required, but the list only has the 26 Swiss cantons. Cross-border employees could not be registered.
options: Canton of residence; ask the fund what to enter for residents abroad
Canton of work (e.g. Zurich), so it is not asked of the employee
open_questions.recommendation: Ask Pensionskasse Muster. Meanwhile ask the canton only of Swiss residents.

open_questions.question: Which permit types should the employee and spouse be able to choose from, and how does a spouse without any permit answer?
open_questions.why_it_matters: No source lists the permits. Only 'C permit' changes the outcome, but the employee needs a list they recognise.
open_questions.recommendation: Ask HR for the list it uses. The rule only needs to tell C permit apart from other permits.

open_questions.question: Is the consolidated source tax rule complete and does 'here' mean Switzerland? HR hedged ('I think so') before adding further conditions.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The rule decides who sees the whole source tax section and the spouse questions. A wrong rule asks Swiss employees too much or misses people who are subject.
open_questions.recommendation: Have HR confirm the decision table of subject_to_source_tax.

open_questions.question: How should employees with several nationalities, one of them Swiss, answer the nationality question?
open_questions.why_it_matters: HR's rule is 'Swiss passport'. Dual nationals could pick their other nationality and be wrongly sent the source tax questions.
options: Ask 'Do you hold Swiss citizenship?' first
open_questions.recommendation: Confirm with HR that any Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss.

open_questions.question: Is a new employee's income always earned income (Erwerbseinkommen), so the income-type question can be fixed instead of asked?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Asking a new hire about replacement income is confusing and collects unnecessary data. Fixing it also removes the replacement-income cross-border variants.
open_questions.recommendation: Fix to earned income by product decision. Until then it is modelled as asked.

open_questions.question: HR says everyone living abroad is subject to source tax, but the calculator can return 'in principle no source tax liability' for Liechtenstein residents. Which result counts?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It affects what HR does after the questionnaire. It does not change which questions are asked.
open_questions.recommendation: Keep asking these employees all source tax questions and let the calculator result decide. Confirm with HR.

open_questions.question: Can a new employee answer 'certificate of residence provided' and 'proof of more than 60 non-return days provided' before starting? To whom are these documents provided?
open_questions.why_it_matters: These questions ask about documents, possibly the 'German forms' HR mentioned. The employee may not have them yet.
options: Ask as yes/no and let HR collect the documents
Ask whether the employee will provide them
open_questions.recommendation: Ask HR how this works today for Stefan.

open_questions.question: Do the child and cross-border paths behave as modelled for every combination? The calculator was only spot-checked for A/B/H cross-border tariffs, more than 3 children, deleting children and special tariffs (e.g. D).

feature.title: Employee onboarding questionnaire
feature.goal: A new employee of Muster AG answers one English questionnaire that asks each piece of information once, and only when Pensionskasse Muster, the Zurich source tax calculator or HR needs it for this person. The answers are enough to complete the pension registration, find the source tax tariff and run HR onboarding without follow-up emails.
feature.context:
Today Muster AG's HR runs onboarding by hand and collects the same data for several receiving parties: the pension fund (Pensionskasse Muster), source tax (Zurich tariff calculator) and HR itself [G-01, G-02]. The sources name these pain points:
- **The first working day is HR's "number one" item and often moves.** The pension insurance start date depends on it and must always be the 1st of a month. When the start day changes, the pension fund's date must be corrected [F-hr_transcript-872bd7, F-hr_transcript-1d5c07, F-hr_transcript-e18e66, F-pension_portal-509cbe].
- **HR cannot tell up front who must answer the source tax questions.** Whether someone is subject to source tax depends on residence, nationality, permit and the spouse's situation. HR collects the spouse details through manual email follow-ups [F-hr_transcript-5af8d0, F-hr_transcript-b84498, F-hr_transcript-b90bd9, F-hr_transcript-a45422].
- **Missing required fields block the pension registration.** For example, the spouse's date of birth is required when the employee is married [F-pension_portal-44a27b, F-pension_portal-c5ee15].
- **Data minimisation forbids asking more than needed.** Sensitive data such as religious denomination must only be asked of employees who are subject to source tax [G-01].
- **The Zurich calculator has a deep tree of questions.** These cover income type, denomination, the spouse, children and cross-border situations for Germany and Liechtenstein, and only a subset applies to each person [F-zh_source_tax_calculator-e06ffd, F-zh_source_tax_calculator-103b19, F-zh_source_tax_calculator-69edd5].

**Scope:** which information is asked, in which order, under which conditions and whether it is required, plus the business rules derived from the answers [G-04].

**Out of scope** [G-03, G-04, F-hr_transcript-7668e6, F-hr_transcript-f23d48]:
- how the data is sent to each party
- AHV data
- IT equipment
- employee badge photos

**Simplifications** [G-05]: Switzerland has exactly one source tax system (Zurich's) and exactly one pension fund (Pensionskasse Muster).

sections.title: Questionnaire flow overview
sections.purpose: Set the steps of the questionnaire, their order and the conditions for showing each step, so every employee sees only the questions that apply to them and answers each one once.

stories.title: Show the source tax step only to employees who are subject to source tax
stories.i_want: to see the source tax questions only if I am actually subject to source tax
stories.so_that: I am not asked for sensitive data (for example my religious denomination) that nobody needs from me, and HR no longer has to send the whole source tax questionnaire to everybody
stories.priority_reason: HR calls source tax its biggest time sink: it sends the whole questionnaire to everybody because it cannot tell up front who must answer, and Swiss employees get annoyed and call HR. Data minimisation also forbids asking sensitive source tax questions of people who are not subject.

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees who are not subject to source tax finish after the Family step
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee whose answers in steps 1 to 5 show that they are not subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax), for example a Swiss national living in Switzerland, a non-Swiss employee with a C permit living in Switzerland, or an employee married to a Swiss or C-permit spouse who lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee completes the Family step (step 5)
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire ends after step 5; the employee sees none of the source tax questions (type of income, denomination, spouse works, children, cross-border questions)

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees who are subject to source tax continue with the Source tax step
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee whose answers in steps 1 to 5 show that they are subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax), for example anybody living outside Switzerland, or a non-Swiss employee in Switzerland without a C permit who is not married to a Swiss or C-permit spouse living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee completes the Family step (step 5)
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire continues with step 6 Source tax, showing only the source tax questions that apply to this employee; the rule itself is still to be confirmed by HR (see OQ-source-tax-rule), and for Liechtenstein residents see OQ-liechtenstein

stories.title: Ask the steps in an order that avoids unneeded questions
stories.i_want: to go through the questionnaire in a fixed order of steps, where earlier answers decide which later questions I see
stories.so_that: I am never asked a question whose answer nobody needs for me, such as my nationality when I live abroad or my spouse's details when I am not married
stories.priority_reason: Enables data minimisation and avoids annoying employees with irrelevant questions; it structures the questionnaire rather than unblocking a registration on its own.

acceptance_criteria.title: The steps follow a fixed order in English
acceptance_criteria.given: any new employee of Muster AG
acceptance_criteria.when: they open the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire is in English and the steps come in this order: 1 Personal details (first name, last name, date of birth); 2 Home address (street, house number, postcode, town, country, and the canton if the employee lives in Switzerland); 3 Employment start (the first working day); 4 Nationality and permit; 5 Family (civil status and, where they apply, spouse questions); 6 Source tax. Steps 4 and 6 and the spouse questions in step 5 appear only under the conditions in the other criteria of this story and in US-01.1's rule

acceptance_criteria.title: Home address comes before nationality; employees living abroad skip step 4
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered their home address in step 2
acceptance_criteria.when: the country of the home address is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: step 4 Nationality and permit is skipped entirely, because employees living abroad are subject to source tax whatever their nationality; if the country is Switzerland, the nationality is asked, and the permit only if the employee is not Swiss (for employees with several nationalities see OQ-dual-nationality)

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status comes before the spouse questions
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is in step 5 Family
acceptance_criteria.when: they have answered their civil status
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's nationality, permit and residence are asked only if the employee is married and would otherwise be subject to source tax (lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss and has no C permit); the spouse's residence is asked only if the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit; otherwise none of these spouse questions appear

Single B-permit employee living in Switzerland
Married Swiss employee living in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: The employee confirms the first working day; the insurance start date is derived
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is in step 3 Employment start
acceptance_criteria.when: the step is shown
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked to confirm their first working day and is not asked for the pension insurance start date; that date is derived from the first working day (rule insurance_start_date)

stories.title: Ask each piece of information once and reuse it for every receiving party
stories.i_want: every piece of information to be asked of the employee only once in the questionnaire, even when several receiving parties need it
stories.so_that: the answers are enough for the pension registration, the source tax tariff and HR onboarding without asking the same thing twice or sending follow-up emails
stories.priority_reason: This is the core promise of the feature: asking too little blocks a registration, asking twice or too much annoys employees and collects data we must not have. Today HR collects the same data by hand for several parties and asks spouse details by email, which takes forever.

acceptance_criteria.title: Information needed by several parties is asked once
acceptance_criteria.given: an information item needed by more than one receiving party, for example the civil status (pension fund and source tax) or the country of the home address (HR's postal address and source tax residence)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the item is asked exactly once, in its step, and the same answer serves every party that needs it; the source tax step does not ask again for civil status or country of residence

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse details are collected in the questionnaire, not by email
acceptance_criteria.given: a married employee who would otherwise be subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: they complete step 5 Family
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse details HR needs for the source tax check are already answered in the questionnaire, so HR does not need to ask for them by email

acceptance_criteria.title: No question without a receiving party
acceptance_criteria.given: any question in the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: it is shown to an employee
acceptance_criteria.then: at least one receiving party in scope (Pensionskasse Muster, the Zurich source tax calculator or Muster AG's HR) needs the answer for this employee; out-of-scope data such as AHV data, IT equipment or badge photos is not asked

sections.title: Personal details and home address
sections.purpose: Collect the employee's identity and complete postal address. The pension registration needs these, HR posts documents to the address, and the country of the address decides which later questions apply.

stories.title: Collect the employee's name and date of birth
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their first name, last name and date of birth in the Personal details step of the onboarding questionnaire
stories.so_that: the occupational pension registration has the required identity fields and is not rejected with 'First name / Last name / Date of birth is required.'
stories.priority_reason: The pension fund's registration form marks these fields as required and blocks submission when they are empty. Missing required fields are a named pain point that blocks the pension registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: First and last name are always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: any new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the Personal details step, which is the first step
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their first name and their last name. Neither may be left empty. Both go to the pension fund, which requires them for the registration, and to HR, which uses them to identify the employee and address documents.

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is always asked, required and given as DD.MM.YYYY
acceptance_criteria.given: any new employee fills in the Personal details step
acceptance_criteria.when: they give their date of birth
acceptance_criteria.then: the date of birth is asked of every employee, may not be left empty, and is given as a date in the form DD.MM.YYYY (e.g. 14.03.1990), the form the pension fund's registration expects. It goes to the pension fund for the registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Personal details are asked once
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has given their first name, last name and date of birth in the Personal details step
acceptance_criteria.when: the pension fund and HR both need these details
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not asked for them again anywhere else in the questionnaire. The same answers serve every receiving party that needs them.

stories.title: Collect a complete postal home address
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their complete home address (street, house number, postcode, town and country) in the Home address step
stories.so_that: HR can post documents to the employee without chasing missing parts of the address
stories.priority_reason: HR says it 'obviously' needs the address and that it has to be complete because it posts many documents to employees. An incomplete address blocks HR's postal onboarding.

acceptance_criteria.title: All five address parts are always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: any new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the Home address step, which follows the Personal details step
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for street, house number, postcode, town and country of their home address. None of these may be left empty, whichever country they live in. The address goes to HR for posting documents.

acceptance_criteria.title: The address is a normal postal address
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee gives their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: they fill in the address parts
acceptance_criteria.then: they write it as a normal postal address, the way it would appear on an envelope. Nothing beyond street, house number, postcode, town and country is asked. The country is given by its English name, e.g. "Switzerland", "Germany" or "Liechtenstein".

stories.title: Use the home address country as the country of residence
stories.i_want: the country of the employee's home address to count as their country of residence
stories.so_that: the questionnaire can tell from the address alone whether the employee lives abroad, and therefore is subject to source tax, without asking for the country of residence a second time
stories.priority_reason: HR cannot tell up front who must answer the source tax questions. Residence abroad alone makes an employee subject to source tax, and this decides which later questions are asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Country of residence is not asked separately
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has given the country of their home address in the Home address step
acceptance_criteria.when: a receiving party needs the employee's country of residence, e.g. for the source tax calculator's 'main residence in Switzerland' and 'country of residence' questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the country of the home address is used as the country of residence, and the employee is not asked for their country of residence again.

acceptance_criteria.title: Living abroad makes the employee subject to source tax, whatever their nationality
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's home address is outside Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire decides whether the employee is subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax)
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is subject to source tax, and they are not asked for their nationality, because it does not change the outcome. Employees whose home address is in Switzerland are asked for their nationality. (Whether Liechtenstein residents really count as subject is open, see OQ-liechtenstein.)

stories.title: Employee confirms the first working day
stories.i_want: every new employee to give or confirm their first working day at Muster AG in the onboarding questionnaire
stories.so_that: the pension registration and HR onboarding start from the date that actually applies, even when it has moved since the contract was agreed (for example because the employee negotiated an earlier exit with their old employer)
stories.priority_reason: HR calls the first working day the 'number one' item; the pension registration cannot be completed without it, and a stale date has already caused a wrong date at the pension fund and weeks of fixing.

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day is always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee of Muster AG fills in the onboarding questionnaire, whatever their residence, nationality, permit or civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the Employment start step
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their first working day at Muster AG and cannot complete the questionnaire without giving it

acceptance_criteria.title: Question makes clear the date must be the currently agreed one
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's first working day may have moved since the contract was signed

acceptance_criteria.then: the question asks them to confirm the first working day as currently agreed with Muster AG, so a date that moved (e.g. after an earlier exit from the old employer) is captured

acceptance_criteria.title: Form of the answer and who receives it
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee answers the first working day
acceptance_criteria.when: the answer is recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: it is a calendar date (shown as DD.MM.YYYY); HR receives it to confirm the agreed start, and it is the basis for the pension fund's insurance start date (see rule insurance_start_date). The employee is never asked for the insurance start date itself.

stories.title: Derive the pension insurance start date from the first working day
stories.i_want: the insurance start date for each new employee to be derived from their first working day and always fall on the 1st of a month
stories.so_that: every registration carries a valid, correct insurance start date without the employee having to know the pension fund's rule

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day on the 1st of a month: insurance starts that day
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's confirmed first working day is the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.when: the insurance start date is determined
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date is the first working day itself

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day not on the 1st: insurance starts on the 1st of the following month
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's confirmed first working day is any day other than the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.when: the insurance start date is determined
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date is the 1st of the month following the first working day, including across a year end

acceptance_criteria.title: Insurance start date is derived, never asked
acceptance_criteria.given: any new employee
acceptance_criteria.when: they fill in the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: they are not asked for an insurance start date; the pension fund receives the derived date, which is always the 1st of a month and given as DD.MM.YYYY as its registration requires

stories.title: Re-derive the insurance start date when the first working day moves
stories.i_want: the insurance start date to be derived again whenever the employee's first working day changes

sections.title: Civil status and spouse data for the pension fund
sections.purpose: Ask the civil status once, using the pension fund's list, and the spouse's date of birth when the employee is married. The source tax calculator's civil status question is answered from the same answer, not asked again.

stories.title: Ask the employee's civil status using the pension fund's list
stories.i_want: every new employee to state their civil status, choosing from exactly the options of my registration form (Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed)
stories.so_that: the required 'Civil status' field of the registration is always filled with a value I accept, and the registration is not blocked
stories.priority_reason: Civil status is a required field of the pension fund registration. Leaving it empty blocks the registration ('Civil status is required.').

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is asked of every employee and cannot be left empty
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee filling in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the Family step
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their civil status, whatever their other answers are. They cannot finish the questionnaire without answering it, because the pension fund registration is blocked without a civil status.

acceptance_criteria.title: Only the pension fund's civil status values can be chosen
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer
acceptance_criteria.then: they choose exactly one of: Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed - the complete list of the pension fund's registration form, with the same wording. No other value is offered. How employees in a registered partnership or separated employees answer is still open (see OQ-registered-partnership and OQ-separated); until it is decided, no extra option is added.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is asked once and serves both the pension fund and source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the answers are used for the receiving parties
acceptance_criteria.then: the same answer fills the pension fund's 'Civil status' field and answers the source tax calculator's civil status question (see rule calculator_civil_status). The employee is never asked a second civil status question for source tax.

stories.title: Ask the spouse's date of birth when the employee is married
stories.i_want: the date of birth of the husband or wife of every married employee, and no spouse date of birth for employees who are not married
stories.so_that: the registration of a married employee is not blocked by an empty 'Spouse's date of birth' field, and no spouse data is collected that I do not need
stories.priority_reason: When civil status is Married, the pension fund blocks the registration if the spouse's date of birth is empty ('Spouse's date of birth is required.').

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's date of birth is asked and required only for married employees
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status is Married
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked for their spouse's date of birth in the Family step and cannot finish the questionnaire without it. The answer goes to the pension fund.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's date of birth is not asked of employees who are not married
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status is Single, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's date of birth is not asked. For Single this matches the pension fund form. For Divorced and Widowed no screenshot shows the form, so this rests on the assumption that no spouse field appears (see OQ-divorced-widowed).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's date of birth is given as a full date
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for their spouse's date of birth
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer
acceptance_criteria.then: the answer is a full calendar date given as DD.MM.YYYY (e.g. 14.03.1988), as the pension fund requires.

stories.title: Answer the calculator's civil status question from the employee's civil status
stories.i_want: the calculator's civil status question ('married or registered partnership' or 'single, divorced, separated, widowed') to be answered from the civil status the employee already gave for the pension fund
stories.so_that: the tariff can be determined without asking the employee a second civil status question
stories.priority_reason: The calculator needs the civil status of every person subject to source tax to find the tariff, and the feature requires asking each piece of information once.

acceptance_criteria.title: Married maps to 'married or registered partnership'
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee answered civil status Married
acceptance_criteria.when: the calculator's civil status answer is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: it is 'Married or registered partnership' (Verheiratet oder eingetragene Partnerschaft).

acceptance_criteria.title: Single, Divorced and Widowed map to 'single, divorced, separated, widowed'
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee answered civil status Single, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.when: the calculator's civil status answer is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: it is 'Single, divorced, separated, widowed' (Ledig, Geschieden, Getrennt, Verwitwet).

acceptance_criteria.title: Registered partners and separated employees follow the open decisions
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee in a registered partnership, or a separated employee who is still married
acceptance_criteria.when: the calculator's civil status answer is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: the result follows the civil status they chose from the pension fund's list. Whether registered partners should choose Married is open (see OQ-registered-partnership). Whether separated employees, who would choose Married and so get 'married or registered partnership', need a separate source tax answer is also open (see OQ-separated). No extra question is asked until these are decided.

acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers
acceptance_criteria.then: the nationality is given as a country by its English name (e.g. "Switzerland", "Portugal") and the permit as e.g. "B permit" or "C permit". Only a C permit changes the outcome; the full list of permits to offer is open (see OQ-permit-list). How employees who also hold Swiss citizenship answer is open (see OQ-dual-nationality). Whether the questionnaire reminds non-Swiss employees to bring their permit on the first day is open (see OQ-permit-reminder).

acceptance_criteria.title: Who uses nationality and permit
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered the nationality and, if asked, the permit type
acceptance_criteria.when: the answers are recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: they are used to decide whether the employee is subject to source tax, so that HR knows up front whether the employee must answer the source tax questions. They are not asked for any other receiving party.

stories.title: Ask the spouse's nationality, permit and residence only when they can exempt the employee
stories.i_want: the questionnaire to ask a married employee for the spouse's nationality, permit and country of residence, but only when the employee would otherwise be subject to source tax
stories.so_that: I no longer have to check the spouse exemption by hand and chase the spouse details by email, and no spouse data is collected when it cannot change the outcome
stories.priority_reason: HR checks the spouse exemption by hand today and asks for the spouse details by email, which 'takes forever'. Getting it wrong sends the source tax questions to the wrong people.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's nationality is asked only of married employees who would otherwise be subject
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has given their home country, nationality, permit (if asked) and civil status (asked in the family step)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee is "Married", lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss and does not hold a C permit
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's nationality is asked and required. It is not asked of employees who are not married, who live abroad, who are Swiss or who hold a C permit, because the spouse cannot change their outcome.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's permit is asked only if the spouse is not Swiss

acceptance_criteria.when: the spouse's nationality is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's Swiss permit is asked. If the spouse is Swiss, the permit is not asked. A spouse may have no permit at all (HR: 'their permit if they have one'); how the employee says so is open (see OQ-permit-list).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's residence is asked only if the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse's nationality was asked (see AC-05.2.1)
acceptance_criteria.when: the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's country of residence is asked and required, because the exemption applies only if that spouse lives in Switzerland. If the spouse is neither Swiss nor a C-permit holder, the spouse's residence is not asked. stories.i_want: Lonio to decide from the employee's answers whether they are subject to source tax
stories.so_that: I know up front who has to answer the source tax questions, and only those employees are asked them
stories.priority_reason: HR 'never knows up front' who must answer the source tax questions. This decision controls the whole source tax section and the data minimisation for sensitive data such as religious denomination.

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living abroad are always subject
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's home address is in a country other than Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether the employee is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is subject to source tax, whatever their nationality. No nationality, permit or spouse questions are needed for this decision. How Liechtenstein residents whom the calculator may treat as not liable are handled is open (see OQ-liechtenstein).

acceptance_criteria.when: the employee is Swiss, or is not Swiss but holds a C permit
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not subject to source tax, whatever their civil status. C-permit holders are treated like Swiss nationals.

acceptance_criteria.title: Non-Swiss employees without a C permit who are not married are subject

acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not subject to source tax only if the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit and lives in Switzerland. In every other case (spouse neither Swiss nor C-permit holder, or Swiss/C-permit spouse living abroad) the employee is subject.

acceptance_criteria.given: Lonio has decided whether the employee is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee would reach the source tax section (income type, religious denomination, spouse employment, children, cross-border questions)
acceptance_criteria.then: an employee who is subject is asked the source tax section. An employee who is not subject is not asked any of it, so sensitive data such as religious denomination is not collected from them. HR can see for each employee whether they are subject. stories.priority_reason: Needed to start the calculator path, but for a new hire the answer is presumably always earned income and may be fixed by a product decision (see OQ-income-type); the source tax pain points are mainly about who answers and the spouse follow-ups.

acceptance_criteria.title: Income type is asked and required only when the employee is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's answers on residence, nationality, permit, civil status and spouse decide whether they are subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax step
acceptance_criteria.then: the type of income question is asked and must be answered if the employee is subject to source tax; it is not asked at all if the employee is not subject. Until the open question OQ-income-type is decided, the question is asked rather than fixed to earned income.

acceptance_criteria.title: Allowed answers for the type of income
acceptance_criteria.given: the type of income question is asked

acceptance_criteria.then: the employee chooses exactly one of "Earned income" or "Replacement income" (the calculator's two options), and the answer is used for the source tax tariff determination.

stories.so_that: the tariff carries the right church-tax suffix (Y or N), while this sensitive information is never collected from employees who are not subject to source tax
stories.priority_reason: The tariff cannot be completed without the suffix, and asking denomination of everyone would breach data minimisation, which the product owner names as a hard constraint (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination is asked only of employees subject to source tax with earned income
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's subject_to_source_tax result and type of income are known
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the denomination question in the source tax step
acceptance_criteria.then: the denomination is asked and must be answered only if the employee is subject to source tax and has earned income; it is not asked of employees who are not subject to source tax, nor of employees with replacement income.

acceptance_criteria.title: Allowed answers for the denomination
acceptance_criteria.given: the denomination question is asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers it
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee chooses exactly one of "Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed" or "None or other" (the calculator's two options); no more detailed denomination is collected. The answer is used only for the source tax tariff.

acceptance_criteria.title: Church-tax suffix is derived from type of income and denomination
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax has answered the type of income and, if asked, the denomination
acceptance_criteria.when: the church-tax suffix of the tariff is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: earned income with "Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed" gives suffix Y; earned income with "None or other" gives suffix N (e.g. A0Y vs A0N); replacement income gives no suffix (tariff G).

stories.title: Ask married employees subject to source tax whether their spouse works
stories.i_want: married employees who are subject to source tax and have earned income to state whether their spouse is gainfully employed or receives replacement income
stories.so_that: I can answer the calculator's spouse question without an email follow-up, and single, divorced or widowed employees are not asked about a spouse
stories.priority_reason: HR names the spouse details as a manual email follow-up that 'takes forever'; without this answer the married tariff (B or C) cannot be determined.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse employment is asked only of married employees subject to source tax with earned income
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's subject_to_source_tax result, type of income and civil status are known
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the spouse employment question in the source tax step (after the denomination question)
acceptance_criteria.then: the question is asked and must be answered only if the employee is subject to source tax, has earned income and has civil status "Married"; otherwise it is not asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Allowed answers for spouse employment
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse employment question is asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers it
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee answers "yes" if the spouse is gainfully employed or receives replacement income, otherwise "no"; the answer is used for the source tax tariff determination.

stories.title: Derive the base source tax tariff letter
stories.i_want: the base tariff letter (A, B, C, G or H) to be derived from the employee's type of income, civil status, spouse employment and counted children
stories.so_that: I know the expected tariff before using the Zurich calculator, which stays the authority for the final tariff
stories.priority_reason: The tariff is the output source tax needs; today HR works it out by hand in the calculator for everybody.

acceptance_criteria.title: Replacement income gives tariff G
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax answered "Replacement income"
acceptance_criteria.when: the base tariff letter is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is G, whatever the civil status.

acceptance_criteria.title: Married employees get C with a working spouse and B otherwise
acceptance_criteria.given: a married employee subject to source tax with earned income answered whether the spouse works (see the spouse employment question)
acceptance_criteria.when: the base tariff letter is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is C if the spouse works or receives replacement income ("yes"), and B if not ("no").

acceptance_criteria.title: Not married employees get A, or H when a child is counted with H
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax with earned income is Single, Divorced or Widowed and has answered the children questions
acceptance_criteria.when: the base tariff letter is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is H if at least one child lives in the household and the employee has sole custody or is the main financial contributor to that child; otherwise it is A.

acceptance_criteria.title: The calculator stays the authority for the final tariff
acceptance_criteria.given: a base tariff letter has been derived

sections.title: Source tax tariff: children
sections.purpose: For employees subject to source tax only, ask whether there are children, then one block of questions per child. Each block asks only what is needed to decide whether that child counts towards the tariff digit or leads to tariff H.

stories.title: Ask about children only of employees who need a source tax tariff
stories.i_want: the employee to say whether they (or, if married, they or their spouse) have biological or adopted children, asked only when the employee is subject to source tax and has earned income
stories.so_that: the Zurich tariff calculator's children questions can be answered without follow-up emails, while employees who are not subject to source tax are not asked about their family (data minimisation)
stories.priority_reason: Without this answer the source tax tariff cannot be determined; HR today cannot tell up front who must answer source tax questions, and data minimisation forbids asking everyone (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Asked only of employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's answers on residence, nationality, permit and spouse decide whether they are subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax, owned by another section) and they have earned income
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire reaches the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the children question is asked, and must be answered, only if the employee is subject to source tax; employees who are not subject never see it

acceptance_criteria.title: Not asked for replacement income
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax whose income type is replacement income

acceptance_criteria.then: the children question is not asked, because the calculator skips all personal and child questions for replacement income (see OQ-income-type on whether a new employee can have replacement income at all)

acceptance_criteria.title: Position and scope of the question depend on civil status
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax with earned income
acceptance_criteria.when: the children question is asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Answer yes or no; yes opens the per-child questions
acceptance_criteria.given: the children question is asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers
acceptance_criteria.then: the answer is "yes" or "no" and cannot be left empty; only "yes" leads to the per-child questions, "no" asks nothing about children; the answer is needed by the source tax office (Zurich calculator)

stories.title: One block per child: age status and household
stories.i_want: for every child the employee declares, to know whether the child is a minor, an adult in first education or neither, and (for the first two) whether the child lives in the employee's household
stories.so_that: children who cannot count towards the tariff are dropped right away and the remaining questions for each child can be narrowed down
stories.priority_reason: These answers decide for every child whether it counts towards the source tax tariff; without them the tariff cannot be determined.

acceptance_criteria.title: A block of questions for each child
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax has answered "yes" to having biological or adopted children (US-07.1)
acceptance_criteria.when: the child questions are asked
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee can describe each child in its own block (Child 1, Child 2, ...) and can add or remove a child; every question of this section is answered per child. How the calculator behaves with more than three children or after removing a child was not checked (see OQ-calculator-coverage)

acceptance_criteria.title: Age status asked for every child
acceptance_criteria.given: a child block
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee describes the child
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must say whether the child is "Minor", "Adult in first education" or "Neither"; the question cannot be left empty and is needed by the source tax office

acceptance_criteria.title: A child who is neither ends its block
acceptance_criteria.given: a child described as "Neither" (not a minor and not an adult in first education)
acceptance_criteria.when: the block is answered
acceptance_criteria.then: no further question is asked for that child, and the child does not count towards the tariff

acceptance_criteria.title: Same household asked for minors and adults in first education
acceptance_criteria.given: a child described as "Minor" or "Adult in first education"
acceptance_criteria.when: the block continues
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer "yes" or "no" to whether the child lives in the same household; it is needed by the source tax office to decide whether and how the child counts

stories.title: Minor child living in the employee's household

stories.so_that: it can be decided whether the child counts towards the tariff digit and, for employees who are not married, whether it leads to tariff H

acceptance_criteria.title: Custody asked; sole custody ends the block
acceptance_criteria.given: a child described as "Minor" who lives in the same household (US-07.2)
acceptance_criteria.when: the block continues
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must choose "Shared custody" or "Sole custody"; with sole custody no further question is asked for that child (the child counts, and for an employee who is not married it leads to tariff H)

acceptance_criteria.title: Shared custody: common household with the other parent

acceptance_criteria.when: the block continues
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer "yes" or "no" to living in a common household with the child's other parent. acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is subject to source tax (anyone living abroad is) and has answered the type of income
acceptance_criteria.when: the country of the home address is Germany
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer 'yes' or 'no' to whether they return daily to their main residence in Germany; employees living in any other country are not asked this question. The answer is needed by source tax only

acceptance_criteria.title: Replacement income asks about the time during or before receiving it
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany, is subject to source tax and has answered 'Replacement income' as type of income
acceptance_criteria.when: the daily-return question is shown
acceptance_criteria.then: it asks whether the employee returned daily to their main residence in Germany during or before receiving the replacement income, and must be answered 'yes' or 'no'

acceptance_criteria.title: Certificate of residence is asked only after a daily return
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany and is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers that they return daily to their home in Germany
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer 'yes' or 'no' to whether a certificate of residence has been provided; with a certificate the cross-border tariff applies, without it the normal tariff. If the employee does not return daily, the certificate question is not asked. Whether a new employee can already answer this before starting, and to whom the certificate is provided, is open (see OQ-proof-documents). The answer is needed by source tax only

stories.title: Liechtenstein: daily return and more than 45 non-return days
stories.i_want: employees who live in Liechtenstein to say whether they return daily to their home there and, if not, whether they have more than 45 work-related non-return days in the calendar year
stories.so_that: the calculator can decide whether the normal tariff applies or whether there is in principle no source tax liability (subject to the double taxation agreement)
stories.priority_reason: HR names Liechtenstein residents as a real case of employees living abroad (F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a); without these answers the calculator gives no result for them.

acceptance_criteria.title: Daily return to Liechtenstein is asked only of Liechtenstein residents
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is subject to source tax (anyone living abroad is) and has answered the type of income
acceptance_criteria.when: the country of the home address is Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer 'yes' or 'no' to whether they return daily to their main residence in Liechtenstein (for replacement income: during or before receiving it); employees living in any other country are not asked. With daily return the calculator gives 'in principle no source tax liability', subject to the double taxation agreement. Whether HR then still treats the employee as subject is open (see OQ-liechtenstein); the questions are asked either way. The answer is needed by source tax only

acceptance_criteria.title: More than 45 non-return days is asked only without daily return
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Liechtenstein and is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers that they do not return daily to their home in Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer 'yes' or 'no' to whether they have more than 45 work-related non-return days in the calendar year (for replacement income: during or before receiving it). 'yes' leads to the normal tariff, subject to the double taxation agreement; 'no' leads to in principle no source tax liability (see OQ-liechtenstein). Employees who return daily are not asked. The answer is needed by source tax only

flow.intro: The questionnaire has 6 steps. Only the questions that apply to the employee are shown, and a step where no question applies is skipped (in practice only steps 4 and 6 can be skipped). The order follows dependencies: the address comes before nationality because employees living abroad need no nationality question, and civil status comes before the spouse questions. The source tax step comes last because it depends on the answers from all earlier steps. Each piece of information is asked once and reused for every receiving party.

steps.title: Personal details
steps.asks: First name, last name and date of birth.

steps.title: Home address
steps.asks: Street, house number, postcode, town and country of the home address; the canton only if the country is Switzerland. The country of the home address is also used as the country of residence.

steps.title: Employment start
steps.asks: The first working day (confirmed if HR already knows it). The pension insurance start date is derived from it and not asked.

steps.title: Nationality and permit
steps.asks: Nationality; the permit type only if the employee is not Swiss.

steps.title: Family
steps.asks: Civil status. If married: the spouse's date of birth. The spouse's nationality only if the employee is married, lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss and has no C permit; the spouse's permit only if the spouse is not Swiss; the spouse's country of residence only if the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit.
steps.shown_to: Everyone (spouse questions only to married employees, as conditioned)

steps.title: Source tax
steps.asks: Type of income; if earned income: religious denomination; if married: whether the spouse works or receives replacement income; whether the employee has children, and for each child a block: age status, same household, and the follow-up custody, household, contributor and maintenance questions depending on the answers. Then the cross-border questions: if living in Germany, daily return, residence certificate (if daily return), reasonableness of daily return and proof of more than 60 non-return days (if no daily return); if living in Liechtenstein, daily return and more than 45 non-return days (if no daily return).
steps.shown_to: Only employees subject to source tax
